bib.title: Lookback Lens: Detecting and Mitigating Contextual Hallucinations in Large Language Models Using Only Attention Maps

question: Can the ratio of attention on the provided context versus newly generated tokens detect, and help mitigate, contextual hallucinations?
hypothesis: Contextual hallucinations are related to the extent to which an LLM attends to the provided context versus its own generations.
contributions: Lookback ratio feature and a linear Lookback Lens detector
Cross-task and cross-model (7B to 13B) transfer without retraining
Lookback Lens Guided Decoding for mitigation

method.summary: A logistic regression over per-head lookback ratios (attention on context / (context + newly generated)) detects contextual hallucinations in LLaMA-2-7B-Chat outputs, using GPT-4o labels. It is then used to pick the best of k sampled chunks during decoding, and transferred to 13B via a linear head mapping.
method.task: contextual hallucination detection (summarization, QA) and classifier-guided decoding

datasets.name: CNN/DM
datasets.split: sampled from the testing set; two-fold validation for source-task scores
datasets.preprocessing: LLaMA-2-7B-Chat greedy responses (max 256 tokens), annotated by GPT-4o for truthfulness and hallucinated spans

datasets.name: Natural Questions (Liu et al. 2024 setup)
datasets.preprocessing: 3 documents per question, gold in the middle between two irrelevant ones

datasets.name: NQ-train
datasets.preprocessing: annotated as the NQ test set

datasets.name: MT-bench
datasets.size: 80 examples (50 general questions for the hallucination variant)
datasets.split: second turn only; first turn from GPT-3.5 responses

models.name: LLaMA-2-7B-Chat
models.heads: 1024 attention heads total (32 per layer, inferred: 1,024 heads over 32 layers)

models.name: Lookback Lens
models.architecture: logistic regression on averaged lookback ratios

models.name: vectara/hallucination_evaluation_model (SoTA NLI)
models.architecture: DeBERTa-v3-base fine-tuned on NLI and summarization data

other.train: fine-tuned on the same CNN/DM and NQ data as an NLI task

training.objective: logistic regression, factual (1) vs hallucinated (0), on span-averaged lookback ratio
training.optimizer: scikit-learn LogisticRegression, default hyperparameters (default L2 penalty), max_iter=1000

other.head_mapping: sklearn LinearRegression (closed-form OLS) from 13B heads (1600) to 7B heads (1024), fit on averaged per-head lookback ratios of training examples; 13B run on 7B outputs
other.span_labels_predefined: non-hallucinated = text before first hallucinated span, after last, or fully non-hallucinated responses; hallucinated spans = negatives
other.span_labels_sliding: all chunks of size 8; label 0 if overlapping any hallucinated span

inference.decoding: data generation: greedy; guided decoding: sample k candidate chunks, pick argmax of F(mean lookback ratio), repeat until EOS or max length
inference.max_tokens: 256 tokens for dataset generation (Appendix A); guided-decoding max length not stated
inference.samples: 8 candidates per chunk; all scores from a single run
inference.prompting: GPT-4o judge prompts (Tables 9-11); LLaMA prompt follows Liu et al. 2024 setup

metrics.name: AUROC
metrics.definition: detection of hallucinated vs non-hallucinated spans/chunks; Train/Test averaged over two-fold validation, Transfer to target task

metrics.name: XSum accuracy
metrics.definition: average of binary GPT-4o judgments of faithfulness

metrics.name: NQ best span exact match
metrics.definition: following Kandpal et al. 2023; Mallen et al. 2023

baselines: hidden states of LLaMA-2-7B-Chat layers 32, 28, 24 (also 20, concatenation, pooling in appendix)
eval.protocol: single run; no confidence intervals or significance test; GPT-4o as judge, checked against humans on 70 XSum and 50 NQ examples

prompts.purpose: GPT-4o truthfulness and span annotation, summarization (CNN/DM, XSum)
prompts.text: You will be provided with a document and a proposed summary. Your task is to determine if the proposed summary can be directly inferred from the document. If the summary contains any information not found in the document, it is considered false.
prompts.where: Table 9 (abridged here; full text in the PDF)

prompts.text: Please act as an impartial judge and evaluate the faithfulness and consistency of the response provided by an AI assistant to the user question displayed below.

evidence.quote: We use all the default hyperparameters, such as L2 penalty, etc, but we change the max_iter to 1000 to ensure it is converged.

results.claim: Predefined spans: Lookback Lens trained on QA transfers to summarization with AUROC 85.3, above the best hidden-state layer (28th, 83.6) and SoTA NLI (76.6).
results.setup: LLaMA-2-7B-Chat greedy outputs (max 256 tokens) on 1,000 CNN/DM and 2,655 NQ examples (3-document context, gold in middle), labels from GPT-4o; logistic regression on 1,024 lookback-ratio features; single run; AUROC; train QA, test Sum. (transfer)
results.table: Table 2, row Lookback Lens QA->Sum., column Transfer (predefined span); rows 28th Layer 83.6, SoTA NLI 76.6

results.claim: Predefined spans, Sum. to QA: Lookback Lens 82.0, but the 28th-layer hidden-state probe scores higher (84.7); SoTA NLI 58.6.
results.setup: LLaMA-2-7B-Chat greedy outputs (max 256 tokens) on 1,000 CNN/DM and 2,655 NQ examples (3-document context, gold in middle), labels from GPT-4o; logistic regression on 1,024 lookback-ratio features; single run; AUROC; train Sum., test QA (transfer)
results.table: Table 2, row Lookback Lens Sum.->QA, column Transfer (predefined span); 28th Layer Sum.->QA 84.7; SoTA NLI QA 58.6

results.claim: Hidden-state probes fit the training task perfectly yet fall in transfer; 24th layer QA to Sum. is 100.0 train and 81.3 transfer.
results.setup: LLaMA-2-7B-Chat greedy outputs (max 256 tokens) on 1,000 CNN/DM and 2,655 NQ examples (3-document context, gold in middle), labels from GPT-4o; logistic regression on 1,024 lookback-ratio features; single run; AUROC; 24th-layer hidden states, predefined spans
results.note: Other layers' QA->Sum. transfer: 32nd 79.4, 28th 83.6. Text: hidden-state classifier 'tends to overfit the training sets during the two-fold validation'.
results.table: Table 2, row 24th Layer QA->Sum., columns Train 100.0, Transfer 81.3

results.claim: Sliding window of 8 tokens (no given spans): Lookback Lens transfer AUROC is only about 66, still above hidden states (56.1-59.4) and NLI.
results.baseline_value: hidden states 56.1-59.4; SoTA NLI 57.1 (Sum.), 61.8 (QA); own NLI 53.0 (Sum.), 64.9 (QA)
results.setup: LLaMA-2-7B-Chat greedy outputs (max 256 tokens) on 1,000 CNN/DM and 2,655 NQ examples (3-document context, gold in middle), labels from GPT-4o; logistic regression on 1,024 lookback-ratio features; single run; AUROC; sliding window = 8; QA->Sum. 66.1, Sum.->QA 66.0

results.claim: Appendix D.2 and D.3: concatenating four hidden-state layers, pooling all 32 layers, or using attention-block outputs does not close the gap (sliding window 8).

results.claim: Lookback Lens guided decoding raises XSum correct rate from 49.0 to 58.6 (reported as a 9.6% gain), on par with SoTA NLI guidance (59.0).
results.setup: Guided decoding: 8 candidate chunks of 8 tokens, classifier trained on CNN/DM only; XSum 1,000 test examples judged by GPT-4o; LLaMA-2-7B-Chat; single run; sampling temperature 0.9, top-p 0.95
results.quote: Lookback Lens Guided Decoding can improve the performance on both in-domain task (XSum, by 9.6%)

results.claim: Hallucinated XSum examples fell from 510 to 414, an 18.8% reduction.
results.setup: Guided decoding: 8 candidate chunks of 8 tokens, classifier trained on CNN/DM only; XSum 1,000 test examples judged by GPT-4o; LLaMA-2-7B-Chat; single run; sampling temperature 0.9, top-p 0.95
results.quote: Our decoding method significantly reduced the number of hallucinated examples from 510 to 414, resulting in an 18.8% reduction in the hallucinated examples.

results.claim: Hidden-state-guided and own-NLI-guided decoding trained on the same data do not improve XSum (28th layer 48.9, own NLI 44.1 vs greedy 49.0).

results.setup: Guided decoding: 8 candidate chunks of 8 tokens, classifier trained on CNN/DM only; NQ 2,655 examples, best-span exact match; LLaMA-2-7B-Chat; single run; sampling temperature 0.9, top-p 0.95

limits: Guided decoding is bounded by the LLM's ability to sample a correct chunk among eight candidates.
Sampling multiple candidates raises inference time (20-30 s per example at 7B).
Needs 1k-2k annotated examples to train the classifier.
All scores are from a single run due to limited compute; no variance reported.
Labels come from GPT-4o, validated on 70 XSum and 50 NQ examples.
Needs attention maps, so only open-weight models; cross-model transfer shown only LLaMA-2 7B to 13B; cross-task plus cross-model decoding (CNN/DM to NQ on 13B) showed no significant gain.
Sliding-window detection (no given spans) is weak for every method (about 66 AUROC at best).
SoTA NLI baseline is trained on far more data (731k), so comparisons are not like-for-like.

terms.definition: the model is provided with the correct facts in the input context but still fails to generate accurate outputs
ratio of attention weights on the given context versus the newly generated tokens, per head: A(context)/(A(context)+A(new))
